newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian state offering 13 pct of Pachin.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian state offering 13 pct of Pachin.

text.p: The state's Holding Company for Chemical Industries said on Wednesday it was offering 13.125 percent of Pachin/Paints and Chemical Industries for sale by auction to at least one anchor investor.

The agent for the auction, Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC), will accept closed bids until 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) on December 25, the parent company said. The bids will be opened at 2.30 p.m. the same day.

Earlier this month the state said it would sell part of its stake in the firm to international investors through global depositary receipts (GDRs) in January. It did not specify how many shares it would offer.
The holding company now has 87.50 percent of the 10 million shares in Pachin and private investors hold the remaining 12.50 percent.
Bids must be for a minimum of 15,000 shares and the price offered should not be less than the closing price on December 17 -- 137.99 pounds ($40.59) a share.
A preliminary guarantee of two percent of the bid's total value, in the form of a bank cheque or letter of credit, should accompany the bid, the holding company said.
Winners will not be eligible for the cash dividend for the financial year 1995/96, it added.
Last week Pachin announced it would pay out a 6.50 pound dividend per share for 1995/6, which ended on June 30.

Pachin's net after-tax profits rose slightly to 103.931 million pounds in 1995/96 from 103.756 million in the previous year, figures provided by the holding company showed. Net sales, however, fell to 285.140 million pounds from 286.386 million.
Shareholders' funds increased to 271.121 million at the end of 1995/96 from 239.639 million one year earlier.
